articles.title: Vision models keep pushing benchmark accuracy — what that means for classifiers like yours
articles.author: Staff Writer
articles.blurb: Latest coverage mapped to your paper’s accuracy story.
body: New image-recognition systems continue to post higher scores on standard classification benchmarks. For researchers reading a CNN classification paper — like the one you uploaded — the headline number is only the start.

What matters next is how the method fails: rare classes, lighting shifts, and examples sitting near decision boundaries. That is the same intuition you practiced in Learn by Doing when a sample flipped from one prototype to another.

Experts note that published accuracy on clear, well-labeled sets can look strong while edge cases remain open. Mapping news to your paper is a reminder to read the limitations section alongside the leaderboard.

articles.title: Why edge cases still break vision systems
articles.author: A. Rivera
articles.blurb: Hard examples near class boundaries — aligned with your Explain step.
body: Production vision stacks still stumble when inputs sit between categories or under unusual conditions. Papers that report strong overall accuracy often leave those failure modes to future work.
Your uploaded demo paper’s story — classify objects, then study mistakes — is exactly the habit practitioners recommend when reading this kind of news.

articles.author: Desk
articles.blurb: How classification models show up outside the lab.
body: From inspection cameras to assistive perception, convolutional classifiers remain a workhorse. News coverage increasingly pairs model claims with evaluation discipline — accuracy plus error analysis.
